value.lineage: do-mpc (2016-, Fiedler/Lucia et al.): nonlinear and robust Model Predictive Control -- at each step solve a finite-horizon optimal-control problem over a model, apply the first input, re-solve (receding horizon); built on CasADi/IPOPT

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: constrained predictive control by receding-horizon optimisation

value.built_to: control a constrained dynamical system by repeatedly solving, at each step, a finite-horizon optimisation over a model of the plant and applying only the first move -- anticipating the future and respecting constraints
value.pressure: hard constraints (actuator/state limits) and a plant where greedy feedback violates them; the controller must look ahead and re-plan as reality diverges from the model
value.success_means: constraint-respecting control that optimises a horizon cost and re-plans fast enough to run in real time

value.pressure: hard state/actuator constraints, model mismatch, a real-time solve deadline
value.failure_condition: the horizon optimisation is infeasible or too slow -> the controller stalls or violates a constraint (a physical limit is breached)

cut.note: receding-horizon control as a symbolic NLP built once and solved every step: the model's ODE/DAE is discretised over the horizon by orthogonal collocation (or a discrete-time map), uncertain parameters branch into a scenario tree whose leaves are weighted equally at each stage (robust multi-stage MPC), the objective sums stage, terminal and input-move costs over scenarios, and at run time only the parameters (x0, previous u, time-varying parameters) change while the solver warm-starts from the last solution; the moving-horizon estimator is the same optimizer class with an arrival cost

organs.human_name: make_step (975-1060): opt_p_num['_x0'], ['_u_prev'], ['_tvp'], ['_p'] set; solve(); u0 = opt_x_num['_u', 0, 0] * scaling; data.update; _x0/_u0 masters updated; _prepare_nlp / _create_nlp build the CasADi problem at setup
organs.mechanism: at setup the whole horizon problem (variables for states, algebraic states, inputs and slacks over N steps and all scenarios; constraints; objective) is assembled as a CasADi expression and handed to a solver (IPOPT by default); at each step the numeric parameter vector is filled with the measured state, the previous input and the time-varying parameters, the NLP is solved starting from the previous solution (warm start), the first input of the first scenario is returned (unscaled), and everything is logged
organs.state: the last solution (warm start), the data log
assumptions: re-solving with a shifted horizon is close to the previous solution, so warm starting keeps the solve fast; the first input is the only one applied (receding horizon)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: nonlinear constrained control at interactive rates; the same object serves simulation and estimation
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: an infeasible NLP at a step returns whatever the solver stopped at (solver_stats are logged for that reason); the initial guess must be set before the first step or the solve is 'likely to fail' (the warning at 1023)
organs.human_prior: MPC (Richalet 1978; Rawlings & Mayne 2009); the CasADi symbolic-NLP route (Andersson et al.)
organs.source_boundary: make_step and the NLP construction entry points

organs.human_name: _setup_discretization (optimizer.py 789-890): collocation_type legendre/radau, degree, ni finite elements; tau_root, the Lagrange polynomial coefficients C, D; the integrator function ifcn; 'discrete' as the alternative
organs.mechanism: each control interval is split into ni finite elements; on each, the state trajectory is a polynomial of the chosen degree interpolating at Legendre or Radau points; the ODE is imposed as equalities at the collocation points (the polynomial's derivative equals the model's f) and continuity at element boundaries; the resulting equations are returned as one CasADi function used per interval and scenario, so the discretised dynamics are constraints of the NLP rather than an integrator called inside it (simultaneous approach)
organs.output: ifcn and the number of collocation points
assumptions: a low-degree polynomial per element resolves the dynamics at the control rate; the simultaneous formulation exposes the dynamics' structure to the NLP solver (sparse Jacobians) instead of hiding it in an integrator
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: stiff nonlinear models handled by the NLP solver's own Newton iterations; exact derivatives by automatic differentiation
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the NLP size grows with degree times elements times scenarios; dummy collocation points exist for the initial state of each branch (the NOTE at 1141)
organs.human_prior: Biegler's simultaneous collocation (2010); the CasADi collocation tutorial

organs.human_name: _prepare_nlp (1105-1220): _setup_scenario_tree; n_max_scenarios = n_combinations ** n_robust; open_loop -> n_u_scenarios = 1; omega = 1/n_scenarios[k+1]; the k (stage) / s (scenario) / b (branch) loops; set_uncertainty_values
organs.mechanism: each uncertain parameter takes values from a user-supplied set; every combination is a branch; the tree branches at each of the first n_robust stages and then stays constant, so the number of scenarios is combinations to the power n_robust; each stage's scenarios are weighted equally in the objective; inputs are per scenario (the controller may react after the uncertainty reveals itself) unless open_loop is set, in which case all scenarios at a stage share the input; the child-scenario bookkeeping lets constraints be imposed on every branch
organs.output: the tree indices and the weights
assumptions: a finite set of parameter realisations spans the uncertainty; branching only for a few stages bounds the exponential growth (the multi-stage compromise)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: constraint satisfaction under parametric uncertainty without the conservatism of min-max over the whole horizon (Lucia et al. 2013)
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: exponential in n_robust; the equal weights are a NOTE in the code ('could be set from outside')
organs.human_prior: Lucia, Finkler & Engell 2013 (multi-stage NMPC); Scokaert & Mayne 1998 for the closed-loop min-max idea
organs.source_boundary: the scenario-tree set-up and the loops that use it

organs.human_name: class MHE(Optimizer, Estimator) (_mhe.py 36-1213): set_objective(stage_cost, arrival_cost), set_default_objective, p_est0, set_y_fun, make_step(y0)
organs.mechanism: over a window of past measurements, the state trajectory and optionally some parameters are decision variables of an NLP whose objective penalises measurement residuals and model residuals per stage plus an arrival cost tying the window's first state to the previous estimate; solving it and taking the last state gives the estimate; the discretisation, scaling and solver machinery are inherited from the same Optimizer base as the controller
assumptions: constrained nonlinear estimation is worth an NLP per step; the arrival cost summarises the discarded past
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: one code path for estimation and control
organs.source_boundary: class MHE; CANDIDATE because the objective assembly was not read

pressures.condition: an organism controls a nonlinear plant with hard state and input constraints; some parameters are unknown within a finite set; measurements arrive each step; the score is cost over a run, constraint violations (fatal) and compute per step
pressures.resource_or_constraint: one NLP solve per step; a scenario budget
pressures.failure_condition: a constraint violation under a realised parameter, or a solve that does not finish within the step
pressures.world_punishes: nominal MPC (violates under the wrong parameter); full min-max over the horizon (too conservative or too big)
pressures.world_rewards: a shallow scenario tree with recourse (inputs per branch) and warm-started re-solves
pressures.observable_consequence: violations and cost over parameter draws for nominal (n_robust = 0), multi-stage (n_robust = 1, 2) and open-loop robust; solve time per step vs tree size
pressures.vacuity_condition: known parameters and no active constraints
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: the true parameter revealed at t = 0 (the cheat control)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the true parameter must achieve the nominal cost with zero violations; nominal MPC on the worst draw must violate; multi-stage with n_robust = 1 must not, at higher cost: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: robust nonlinear MPC (Lucia et al. 2013; do-mpc 2016-)
